Virtual Desktop Security

Practices, controls, and technologies used to secure virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) and virtual desktops in cloud and on-premises environments against unauthorized access, data leakage, and malware.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Virtual Desktop Security?

In this glossary, Virtual Desktop Security refers to: Practices, controls, and technologies used to secure virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) and virtual desktops in cloud and on-premises environments against unauthorized access, data leakage, and malware.

How is Virtual Desktop Security used in cybersecurity?

In cybersecurity communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Implement strong authentication, malware protection, and session isolation controls as part of a comprehensive virtual desktop security strategy."

Why does Virtual Desktop Security matter in cybersecurity?

Virtual Desktop Security matters because it supports clear communication in Cloud contexts for SOC Analysts, Security Engineers, and Incident Responders. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as CISSP, CompTIA Security+, and CEH.

Who uses Virtual Desktop Security?

Virtual Desktop Security is mainly used by SOC Analysts, Security Engineers, and Incident Responders.

What category does Virtual Desktop Security belong to?

In this glossary, Virtual Desktop Security is grouped under Cloud. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.
